name: Antelope Data Center
notes: County amended its zoning in 2025 to allow data centers and data center power plants. Several public hearings (155 commenters); unanimous CUP approval. County then imposed 180-day moratorium on new applicants.

name: Brightspeed Data Center
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Beaver Dam Meta Data Center
notes: NDA with shell companies. Predevelopment agreement (Jul 2024) and TIF district (Nov 2024) approved with agendas that did not mention a data center; public learned in Feb 2025 after annexation/rezoning were done. Formal hearings held, but the project was effectively undisclosed.

name: EdgeConneX Norfolk
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: DIGITAL STERLING PREMIER
notes: Inferred from county rules: data centers were by right in several districts (e.g., IP, GI) until March 2025. Parcel zoning not verified.

name: CyrusOne Fairfield
notes: Texas counties lack zoning. The phase 1 tax abatement hearing was the county's only lever; CyrusOne withdrew its phase 2 abatement request (Jun 2026), removing the hearing. County judge: the abatement was 'our only way to have any say.'

name: Dulles Cloud South Data Center
notes: Comp plan amendment plus rezoning A-1 to PBD (~1,940 ac). Board voted 8-0 not to initiate. Site was outside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay, where data centers were by right until the Sept 22, 2026 amendment. Coalition to Protect PWC organized.

name: DSM14
jur: City of West Des Moines, IA
notes: Microsoft's newer WDM campuses follow a pattern of annexation, light-industrial rezoning, a TIF-backed development agreement and council site plan approval. DSM14 not matched to a specific campus. City required reduced peak water use before approving a sixth campus.

name: Eight Form Data Center
notes: Hotel-to-data-center conversion (50 MW). Plans filed ~6 days before the hearing; 100+ attendees and 700+ pages of comments. Developer withdrew at the end of the 3-hour hearing.

name: Project Aggie
notes: Land already zoned industrial; the veto point was a sale of city-owned land, not zoning. Council rejected the sale unanimously after ~6 hours of comment and a 5,000-signature petition. City signed an NDA in Nov 2024.

name: MANASSAS NCP LLC
notes: Inferred: likely inside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay (by right 2016 to Sept 2026), or in the independent City of Manassas. Parcel not verified.

name: Monterey Park Data Center
notes: Staff treated data centers as a permitted "data processing facility" (no rezoning); design review plus a CEQA MND vote were pending. Stopped via moratorium, urgency ordinance, and a voter-approved citywide ban (Measure NDC, 86%, Jun 2026).

name: Pittsylvania County Data Center
notes: Agricultural to industrial rezoning for 12 buildings plus gas plant. First, larger application withdrawn Nov 2024 after opposition. Board refused the developer's last-minute withdrawal, held the hearing, denied 6-1. Organized coalition plus SELC health study.
tac: Organized group; Coalition (civil rights/env/labor); Expert counter-analysis

name: Project Taurus
notes: Use permitted by zoning; development plan modification approved administratively with no planning commission or council hearing. Residents' only venue was an appeal: planning commission denied it 6-2 after ~16 hours; council appeal postponed (Sept 2026). City designated it a "Rapid Response Project" for expedited review.

name: Digital Realty Northern Virginia IAD35
notes: Inferred from county rules: data centers were by right in several districts (e.g., IP, GI) until March 2025. Parcel zoning not verified.

name: Microsoft Alviso Data Center
notes: Site development permit and parking exception approved by the planning commission; the environmental review (EIR) ran through the state Energy Commission's Small Power Plant Exemption (2022). Air district flagged the Alviso area's high cumulative pollution burden (CalEnviroScreen).

name: Oxford Quantum Circuits Data Center
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: San Marcos Data Center
notes: Also needed a comprehensive plan amendment. P&Z recommended denial (Mar 2025); council vote 5-2 in favor (Aug 2025) failed supermajority. Refiled; P&Z recommended approval (Jan 2026); council denied 5-2 after ~9-hour hearing with hundreds attending.

name: Voltcore Bitcoin Mine
notes: No county zoning; town of Somerville never adopted zoning. County and town moratoriums are unenforceable. Residents' only leverage was refusing utility easements; developer rerouted through county right-of-way.

name: Microsoft South Hill Campus
notes: DCD reports a zoning request filed and approved in early 2021. Deciding body and hearing not confirmed.

name: Ekron Data Center
notes: Ag/residential to light industrial (~138 ac). P&Z unanimously recommended denial after a hearing with 150 sign-ups; Fiscal Court unanimously denied the same day. End user undisclosed.

name: DeForest QTS Data Center
notes: ~1,600 ac annexation from Town of Vienna. QTS withdrew comp plan/rezoning before the scheduled P&Z hearing; board rejected annexation 7-0 after QTS would not meet pre-annexation terms (e.g., 70% renewable). Organized group: No Data Center in DeForest.

name: CyrusOne Data Center
notes: Rezoning plus PUD for 228-ac campus. First of many projects in Yorkville's ~3,000-ac "data center alley"; later projects were approved over P&Z denial recommendations, and residents sued over notice for Project Cardinal.

name: QTS Manassas DC 5
notes: Inferred: QTS Manassas campus appears to be inside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay, where qualifying data centers were by right (2016 to Sept 2026). Parcel not verified.

name: Ransom Township Data Center
notes: Requested a data center overlay district (quarry site zoned conservation). Township supervisors denied 2-1 on a nonsuit motion by a residents' attorney. Developer appealed, arguing exclusionary zoning (PA must allow all legitimate uses).

name: Wildcat Ridge Data Center
notes: Nine conditional use hearings before borough council (Jan-Sep 2026); written decision due within 45 days. Council raised the industrial height limit to 90 ft in Nov 2025 over objections; developer's request that council recuse was denied.

name: Project Spalding
notes: AR-1/R-2 to C-1C plus special exceptions (~133 ac). Rezonings approved 4-1, special exceptions unanimous, with conditions (buffers, generator noise, decommissioning). A resident complained of little public discussion beforehand.

name: Cabin Field Road Data Center
notes: KEY CASE. Request to remove a proffered site plan denied 5-2 (660 petition signatures). But data centers are by right in Industrial-Heavy; the zoning administrator then found scaled-back plans comply with the existing proffer, reopening a by-right path. Only a quasi-judicial appeal remained.

name: Eagle Rock Jones County
notes: 634-ac agricultural rezoning withdrawn <24h before the P&Z hearing after "No Data Centers in Jones County" mobilized; county then adopted a 90-day moratorium. Same developer's Twiggs County project was approved and is being sued over notice and skipped regional review.

name: Spring Valley Technology Park
notes: TR-10 to Industrial Park (325 ac) in the Transition Policy Area. Planning commission unanimously recommended denial (Jul 23, 2026); Board of Supervisors hearing TBD.

name: Oneonta Data Center
notes: Planned Development District rezoning from residential-agricultural. Multiple hearings; ~700 petition signers. Town adopted a 12-month moratorium (May 2026) and is drafting a prohibition.

name: Google Data Center
notes: On TVA-owned land at the retired Widows Creek plant; deal assembled by state, TVA and county EDA. Alabama counties generally lack zoning authority (see Morgan County case), but not verified for this site.

name: Project Liberty
notes: Site in county industrial park. Approval vehicle was a FILOT incentive ordinance passed over three readings under NDAs, without identifying the project as a data center; community meetings came only afterward, without elected officials. Later cancelled, citing utility timing.

name: Amazon Lusby Data Center
notes: Site zoned heavy industrial; AWS filed an administrative conceptual site plan. Commissioners repeatedly rejected a moratorium, then all three lost June 2026 primaries to anti-data-center candidates; AWS withdrew in Aug 2026. Elections substituted for a hearing.

name: Tract Data Center
notes: Planning board recommended denial (Oct 2024), then approval 4-3 (Apr 2025). Withdrawn before the Sept 2025 town board hearing. Tract's business model is entitling land so data centers become by right for end users.

name: CyrusOne: SAT5-SAT6
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: EdgeConneX Data Center/ Hickman Property
notes: Also a comp plan amendment (~700 ac). P&Z unanimously recommended denial; board denied 4-1. Second denial for the property in seven months; site in the Dog River Basin (county reservoir).

name: Jeremiah A QTS Data Center
notes: PUD rezoning of ~800 ac near Wheeler High School. An informational session (no vote) drew 1,000+ people; QTS withdrew before formal hearings.

name: Atlanta-Alpharetta
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Amazon AWS IAD - 23005 International Drive Data Center
notes: Inferred from county rules: data centers were by right in several districts (e.g., IP, GI) until March 2025. Parcel zoning not verified.

name: Edged Data Center

name: LFF Industrial

name: Solstice Data Center
notes: 26 MW edge facility on industrial land; preliminary site plan before the planning commission, which postponed several times and then denied 7-2. Site in 78th percentile of MiEJScreen (area to the east in 98th). City declined a moratorium while the application was pending, to avoid appearing to target it.

name: Prosperity Drive Data Center
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Marrietta Data Center
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Atlas Power

name: La Pine Data Center
notes: Site in county/city-owned industrial park; veto point was the land sale (needed city and county approval). Residents mobilized within weeks of the proposal surfacing; council voted unanimously not to pursue the sale. Developer is a Bitcoin mining firm.

name: Core Scientific Dalton 1 & 2 Data Center Campus
jur: City of Dalton / Whitfield County, GA
notes: Dalton 1 & 2 occupy a vacant factory on Industrial South Road (2018), apparently a permitted industrial use. Contrast: the company's later greenfield Old Tilton Road campus needed a rezoning, approved 3-2 (Mar 2025) on the chair's tie-break over loud opposition; tax abatements via the joint development authority.

name: Rowan AUS01
notes: Annexation, zoning and development agreements approved unanimously (Sept 2025); later phases, abatements and utility agreements approved Sept 2026 over sustained opposition. City then required conditional use permits for future standalone data centers.

name: Project Flo
notes: 468 ac ag/residential to special commercial district. Filed via shell company Deep Meadow Ventures; Google revealed only in Jul 2025. Metropolitan Development Commission approved 8-1; Google withdrew minutes before an expected council denial. A councilor had signed an NDA.

name: Wilmington Data Center
notes: Rezoning, data center use and generator-noise ordinances plus site plan and abatement. Residents sued: federal judge ordered the city to redo the ordinances over defective notice and granted residents expert testimony and cross-examination rights. Ohio Supreme Court blocked a citizen ballot measure (Sept 2026).

name: Project Triton
notes: Planning commission reviewed plans (Jul 2025); council vote was pending. At a town hall a resident exposed false statements by the developer's CEO (undisclosed lawsuit and failed project); city ended the project days later. Pathway type unclear.

name: Agincourt
notes: Redevelopment Commission granted a purchase option on city land (zoned open space; rezoning would be needed). Data center use surfaced via a local conservation group, not the city; after hours of comment at council, developer withdrew and mayor apologized for communication.
tac: Organized group; Packed hearings; Utility/land/water leverage

name: Diode Ventures Data Center
notes: 515 ac ag to light industrial plus SUPs. Planning commission recommended approval (May 2025); board deferred twice after 2.5+ hours of comment; developer withdrew days before the vote. End user never identified.

name: Geronimo Power Data Center
notes: Needs a zoning ordinance change to allow a data center in an agricultural-preservation area, plus an AUAR environmental review. 300+ attended the April hearing. Contrast case: developer ran an aggressive publicity campaign and $30M community fund rather than secrecy.

name: Project Springbank
notes: A-1 to business park (630 ac). Planning commission recommended denial; developer withdrew before the commissioners' vote (county says this is standard practice).

name: Meta Data Center
notes: Land already annexed and zoned industrial (2020), so no public comment was required. Residents complained of being blindsided by the announcement. A later Diode project in Kuna needed a rezoning and passed 3-2 on the mayor's tie-break (Apr 2025).

name: Georgetown Data Center
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

Developer sued for exclusionary zoning; township settled via a court consent judgment (Oct 2025) that let the project proceed, with $14M in community payments. Later rezoning was rescinded, blocking a resident referendum. Residents' Open Meetings Act challenge was rejected.

name: Crow Holdings Development
notes: Zoning already allowed a data center; P&Z denied the site plan (Jan 2026). Developer appealed to council, then withdrew (Mar 2026) after the city banned new data centers in every district (Mar 5, 2026).

name: COPT DC 19 LLC
notes: Inferred: likely inside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay, where qualifying data centers were by right (2016 to Sept 2026). Parcel not verified.

name: Kalkaska Data Center
notes: Proposed on 1,440 ac of state DNR land; the veto point was a state land purchase, which DNR rejected and legislators opposed. Local officials supported it. Developer-hosted forums drew overflow opposition; developer also cited anonymous threats. Withdrawn before any formal land-use process.

name: Blakely Data Center
notes: R-1 (strictest residential) to commercial, ~200 ac. After a heated info session and 1,800+ petition signatures, developers withdrew days before the formal hearing when the borough refused a second informational meeting. Borough then limited data centers to one area as a conditional use.

name: Fermi America HyperGrid/ Project Matador
notes: 99-year ground lease of ~5,800 ac of Texas Tech University System land ("sovereign" state land) in an unincorporated county; no local land-use approval. Amarillo's water agreement was discussed in closed session; lease details obtained only via records request.

name: QTS Atlanta Fayetteville Campus/ Project Excalibur
notes: 412 ac annexed and rezoned R-70 to Business Park (Jun 2022), then site plan approved (Feb 2023). Same city later banned data centers (Mar 2026) and blocked the Crow Holdings project, a useful within-city before/after comparison.

name: Black Pearl Data Center
notes: Inferred: Texas counties lack general zoning authority (see Freestone County case). Site-level approvals and incentives not verified.

name: MS Solar Grid Data
notes: Needed rezoning from single-family to C-2; only the required neighborhood meeting was held, no application filed. Council passed a one-year citywide ban 6-0. New Orleans East is predominantly Black and Vietnamese American; advocates framed it as environmental racism.

name: Digital Realty Northern Virginia IAD24
notes: Inferred from county rules: data centers were by right in several districts (e.g., IP, GI) until March 2025. Parcel zoning not verified.

name: Meta Data Center
notes: Site in Sage Mill Industrial Park (use presumably permitted). County council passed incentive ordinances in Apr 2023 for "Project Sabal"/Starskey LLC; Meta was revealed only at the Aug 2024 announcement.

name: Jeremiah B QTS Data Center
notes: Second site of the same QTS PUD rezoning as Jeremiah A (see DC0416). Coded identically.

name: Project Harper
notes: City had amended its light industrial code to add data centers (a text amendment that would have made the project effectively by right). After a 1,000-member resident campaign, aldermen unanimously removed data centers from the code (Oct 2024). An alderman said staff misled the board about what a data center was.

name: Iron Mountain Data Center
notes: Underground facility in a former limestone mine used for records storage since the 1950s; approvals predate the data center era. No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: BLE Landholdings Data Center
jur: City of Pacific / Franklin County, MO
notes: Jurisdiction shopping: sought annexation/PUD in Pacific and a separate county rezoning. Developer tabled at the Feb 2026 city hearing, leaving residents unable to speak; withdrew after the city adopted a 12-month moratorium. County P&Z reportedly recommended denial; county process status unclear.

name: Stack Infrastructure NVA02A
notes: Inferred: likely inside the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay, where qualifying data centers were by right (2016 to Sept 2026). Parcel not verified.

name: Karis Data Center
notes: Tracker lists Dundee; likely the Karis Critical campus in adjacent Hoffman Estates (verify). Rezoning to a new zoning district withdrawn after controversy; resident filed Open Meetings Act complaint citing emails coordinating private developer access to officials before going public.

name: Vulcan Infrastructure and Power Inc (formerly Greenidge Generation Yates County facility)
notes: Bitcoin mining added to an existing gas power plant under its old permits; no local land-use approval at issue. The veto point was the state Title V air permit: DEC denied renewal in 2022 (~4,000 comments; Seneca Lake Guardian, winemakers), a court annulled the denial in 2024, and DEC settled in Nov 2025.

name: Prologis
notes: 554 ac ag to Industrial-3 for Prologis. Area Plan Commission recommended denial 8-0; commissioners denied 3-0. 1,000+ petition signatures; residents cited farmland and the local Amish community ("Keep Leesburg Rural").

name: Amazon Sunbury Data Center
notes: Land rezoned to limited industrial in 2023 (two hearings) and a 30-year tax abatement approved for Amazon in Nov 2024; a further 330-ac rezoning was pending when council unanimously adopted a moratorium to Jan 2027. Residents also petitioning for a ballot measure capping data centers at 25 MW.

name: Roosevelt Building
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Lumen College Park
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Microsoft Data Center
notes: County administrator says most county data centers went into county-developed industrial sites prepared ~20 years earlier; only recent ones needed rezonings. Inferred by right; Microsoft's 2010 Boydton campus came with state and local incentives.

name: Western Hospitality Partners Data Center
notes: Pekin sold a city-owned farm (~321 ac) to Western Hospitality Partners; the city had sole zoning authority after annexation, over Groveland Township objections. 2,000+ petition signatures and a 5,000-member opposition group; developer withdrew (May 2026).

name: American Tower Data Center
notes: 4 MW edge facility at an existing cell tower in a residential zone, before the Planning and Zoning Board (use variance assumed; verify). 5,800+ petition signatures; township adopted a data center ban while the application was pending; applicant withdrew before the June 30 hearing.

name: Project Agate
jur: City of Conover / Catawba County, NC
notes: Part of a 2022 county-city incentive package for four Microsoft campuses; officials acknowledge public interest was minimal at the time. Construction restarted 2026 amid water-restriction concerns. Site-level zoning not verified.

name: Mall-O-Manor LLC Data Center
notes: ~1,000 ac farmland near New Carlisle (Western Hospitality Partners-linked; end user undisclosed). Area Plan Commission unfavorable; council denied 7-2 after a 10-hour meeting despite a developer PR blitz. A councilwoman reported being "swatted" during the hearing. Amazon's large campus is already nearby.
tac: Packed hearings; Disclosure demands; Expert counter-analysis

name: Muncy Data Center
notes: KEY CASE. Conditional use application filed Apr 2026; township failed to hold the required hearing within 60 days, so the developer claimed "deemed approval" by operation of state law. Supervisors had initially denied that any application existed. Neighbors appealed and joined a constitutional challenge to the deemed-approval rule.

name: STJ Data Center
notes: Annexation hearing (May 2026) held before the city confirmed the use was a data center. Rezoning request withdrawn; council adopted a 12-month pause 8-0, then rejected a citizen advisory committee 3-6.

name: Denver 1 QTS Data Center
notes: Industrial zone where data centers are a permitted use approved administratively; council approved a sales/use tax rebate (Apr 2023). Site is in a census block disproportionately impacted by pollution; a state air permit for 98 more diesel generators is pending.

name: Tract Data Center
notes: 744 ac ag to I-2 with conditional use planned development. Staff recommended approval; planning commission unanimously recommended denial; Tract withdrew, planning to refile. Meanwhile the county's own EDA rezoned other sites for Google data centers in western Chesterfield.

name: Imperial Data Center
notes: KEY CASE. After delays in the City of Imperial, developer moved the project to adjacent county industrial land, where the county treated it as ministerial (no CEQA review); only a lot merger went to the board. City of Imperial and Sierra Club sued; judge tentatively ordered environmental review. Developer sued city officials, activists and journalists, and got the county moratorium struck down. Majority-Latino region.
tac: Legal challenge; Moratorium push; Coalition (civil rights/env/labor)

name: Deep Green Data Center
notes: 24 MW downtown facility on city parking lots, needing both a rezoning and a sale of city land. Public hearing Mar 2026; developer withdrew hours before the council vote, reportedly lacking votes for the land sale. Council then considered a moratorium.
tac: Moratorium push; Utility/land/water leverage; Expert counter-analysis

name: Diode Ventures Data Center
notes: Texas county with no zoning power (county passed a ceremonial resolution asking the Legislature for authority). Leverage came from the local water utility (5M gal/day request from Cedar Creek Lake) and escalation to the governor, who publicly endorsed the withdrawal. Lakeside residential community.

name: Starwood Digital Ventures/ Project Washington
notes: County rezoning pending; county exempted the project from new data center rules. But DNREC ruled it a prohibited heavy-industrial use under the state Coastal Zone Act (516 diesel generators), and a state board unanimously upheld that. Developer appealing to Superior Court; union PLA and PR campaign on developer's side.

name: Switch Pyramid Data Center
notes: Conversion of the former Steelcase Pyramid office building. The decisive approval was a state legislative tax exemption fast-tracked for Switch (2015); township welcomed it. Local land-use approvals not found. Promised 1,000 jobs; 26 by 2022.

name: Sharon Data Center
notes: Former Westinghouse brownfield (earlier a bitcoin mine) in a manufacturing district, where "nothing prevents a data center." Zoning board approved with conditions (70 dB limit, no river water); council approved land development plans. In the state Permit Fast Track program; grandfathered from new county rules.

name: Karis Critical Data Center
notes: Site zoned office/research; CUP needed. Planning and Zoning Commission approved 8-1 (Nov 2025); council overturned it 6-1 after 3+ hours of comment and a 3,700-signature petition, citing health, noise and inconsistency with the master plan. Affluent suburb; developer had cut the project from 72 MW to 24 MW.

name: Markely Data Center
notes: Existing facility (2015 factory conversion with a council-approved $77M tax break) in the Sacred Heart neighborhood, a state-designated Environmental Justice community. Expansion via state air permits for diesel generators; residents (with Yale clinic and CLF) won a court order pausing new generators. City adopted a 360-day moratorium.
tac: Legal challenge; Moratorium push; Coalition (civil rights/env/labor)

name: New Brunswick Data Center
notes: Council voted against allowing a data center on a redevelopment site, requiring a park instead. Redevelopment-plan process; details not verified.

name: Project Spero
notes: Up to $3B project dropped after county officials denied tax abatements (per DCD reporting on a nearby project). Site-level details not verified.

name: MSP1 Data Center
notes: Possibly the Swervo/IronGate Unisys building, where the city denied an interim use permit for chillers, adopted a moratorium, and the developer sued (2026). Identity not verified. name: Irongate Data Center (Swervo)
notes: Conversion of a vacant factory; data centers not permitted in light industrial, so a zoning text amendment plus CUP were needed. name: Caledonia Data Center

name: Menomonie Data Center

Under pressure (10,000-member Facebook group), the mayor refused the development agreement, halting the project.

name: Treetop Development Project
notes: Developer had a warehouse application pending; a 1 GW data center plan surfaced only through a grid-operator filing, with no notice to the town. Town board unanimously adopted a 3-year moratorium (Jun 2026).

name: Atlanta-Douglasville 1

name: Roundhouse Data Center

name: Sabey Data Centers - Columbia
notes: No public record of the approval process found in news or government sources; likely a permitted use in existing commercial/industrial zoning (often an existing-building conversion). Verify via municipal permit records or parcel zoning.

name: Townsite Solar 2 LLC (same as Clearway project that is now canceled?)
